name: Lugh, Many-Skilled Radiance
loreTies: Lugh embodies many-skilled radiance, spear mastery, craft excellence, and heroic brilliance within Avalora.
The Silver-Root Gate allows this deity to enter Ascension-era dungeon routes without collapsing the individuality of other Realms.
Tuatha culture, symbols, weapons, and divine law shape every ability, artifact, silhouette, and combat choice.
shortBackstory: Lugh, Many-Skilled Radiance, is a playable god in Mythos Gates: Ascension. Lugh is the true source-realm divinity behind the mythology — many-skilled radiance, spear mastery, craft excellence, and heroic brilliance. Ascension expands divine power during the current Gate crisis; it does not turn a mortal into a god.

chapters.title: Divine Origin
chapters.text: Lugh is not a mortal hero inspired by myth. Lugh is the actual god recognized by Tuatha source culture, born from the supernatural laws of Avalora. Their domain — many-skilled radiance, spear mastery, craft excellence, and heroic brilliance — determines their symbols, weapons, posture, combat instincts, and relationship to sacred authority.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Within Tuatha, Lugh expresses the civilization rather than merely representing it. Their visual identity must carry the materials, beauty standards, divine symbols, and sacred rules of Avalora. Their gameplay role, Artillery, must grow from mythology first and mechanics second.

chapters.title: Mythos Gate Wound
chapters.text: During the Ascension era, Lugh can interact with The Silver-Root Gate because divine beings are intrinsically connected to their Realms. The Gate does not become a simple teleportation portal; it is a mysterious boundary where separate mythological realities become traversable. Lugh understands some rites of crossing, but not the complete origin of the Mythos Gates.

chapters.title: Dungeon Role
chapters.text: When selected by the player, Lugh enters the dungeon alone as one god or goddess against multiple enemies. No army follows. No squad shares control. Every room, trap, shrine, relic, elite, and boss encounter must test how many-skilled radiance, spear mastery, craft excellence, and heroic brilliance survives pressure from creatures, rival Realm laws, and unstable Gate conditions.

chapters.title: Ascension Conflict
chapters.text: Ascension is the current story arc, not the permanent end-state of the Mythos Gates universe. For Lugh, Ascension means restoration, awakening, evolution, or expansion of existing divine power. Their personal conflict is to recover strength without reducing Tuatha mythology into raw fuel for the crisis.

relationshipHooks: Faction witnesses interpret how Lugh crosses The Silver-Root Gate.
Rival deities challenge the limits of cross-Realm travel.
Dungeon lore pickups reveal Gate mystery without resolving the full origin.
developmentStatus: Playable deity backstory aligned to Mythos Gates identity, one-deity dungeon runs, current Ascension arc, and preserved Lore Codex canon.
mythicSource: source culture humans later copied as Celtic and Irish fae myth
visualCanon: Maeve is Avalora’s root-memory voice. Her silver-branch regalia, thorn records, moss-veiled cloak, crow omen marks, and calm dangerous beauty should feel like the origin behind later fae queens and druid archives.
title: Many-Skilled Radiance

mythosGatesCanon.identityRule: Lugh is the actual god of Tuatha source mythology, never a mortal hero or generic champion.
mythosGatesCanon.arcRule: Ascension restores, awakens, evolves, or expands existing divine power; it does not make the character a god for the first time.
mythosGatesCanon.mysteryRule: The backstory may reveal how this deity interacts with the Mythos Gates, but must not resolve the full origin of the Gates.
